derivationRule: A vector is hand-derived when both of these hold: (a) Judgments are written by a person. Every judgment the contract leaves to a reader is written by a person from the contract text. That covers the token boundaries, classes and texts; inserted tokens; the outcome status; and the error code and the position of the defect. For matching vectors it also covers which regions match, and the outcome. (b) Arithmetic is computed and rechecked. Everything that is pure arithmetic over those judgments is computed by the specification's own checker or builder, which is not an implementation under test. That covers byte spans located from the hand-written token texts, SHA-256 hashes, window selection, fingerprints, digests and canonical bytes. At least one independent recomputation, by a clean-room reviewer or a second checker, confirms it. A vector whose lexical layer was first produced by a tool and then reviewed is not hand-derived, and must be labelled otherwise. Applied to these vectors: every token's class and text, and every inserted semicolon, is written by hand from spec/extraction.md as a literal list in build_vectors.py (HAND_TOKENS), as in ../extraction/harness/build_vectors.py. The arithmetic over those judgments (byte spans, normalized values, k-gram hashes, window selections and fingerprints) is computed by this specification's own builder, not by an implementation under test, and is independently recomputed by ../extraction/check_vectors.py and check_matching.py. A span is located by searching for the token's hand-written text in source order, except in vectors marked spanStarts: hand, where a hand-written start replaces a search that would land inside a comment. The builder's mini-lexer lex() is kept only as a cross-check and must produce the same tokens; it produces no expected value.
lexingCheck: New synthetic inputs for the matching vectors. Token streams are hand-written literals (HAND_TOKENS in build_vectors.py); its mini-lexer lex() is only a cross-check that must agree. Re-verified by ../extraction/check_vectors.py; see README.md.
